title: 2026 Open Letter from the Alliance of CEO Climate Leaders before COP31
gist: The WEF Alliance of CEO Climate Leaders' pre-COP31 open letter argues the low-carbon transition is a strategic economic opportunity, citing market-size projections and 12% green-revenue CAGR, and calls on governments for stable policy and on business for demand signals.

insights.claim: Alliance members (125+ organizations, $4tn revenue) cut aggregate Scope 1-2 emissions about 34% from 2019 to 2024, with Scope 3 the remaining opportunity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum

insights.claim: Green revenues grew at a 12% CAGR in 2020-2024, twice conventional revenues, and the green market, above $5 trillion in 2024, is projected at $7.1 trillion by 2030.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Alliance-sourced growth claim for sustainability-linked sectors.

insights.claim: Projected 2030 market sizes: low-carbon energy above $3.7 trillion, adaptation $1.6 trillion, circular economy $0.5 trillion, sustainable agriculture and land use $200 billion.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum

insights.claim: About 70% of industrial firms surveyed by the IEA reported returns above 10% on efficiency investments, efficiency gains reached 1.8% in 2025 and efficiency investment is expected near $800 billion in 2025, up 70% since 2015.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Efficiency is a high-return capex category.

insights.claim: Climate impacts could cut global GDP by up to 22% by 2100, with mitigation and adaptation investment preventing 10-15 percentage points of that loss.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Macro-damage estimate used to justify adaptation spend.

insights.claim: Solutions like low-carbon fuels, green hydrogen, advanced bioenergy, carbon management and AI optimization are near commercialization but not yet scaled, and need demand signals, policy, manufacturing capacity and public-private finance as solar, wind and storage had.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Next-generation climate tech depends on lead-market creation.

insights.claim: The CEOs ask governments for stable policy frameworks, blended finance and guarantees, scaled international climate finance toward the Baku to Belém Roadmap target of at least $1.3 trillion annually by 2035, Article 6 carbon markets, faster permitting and grid/storage investment.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy agenda items to watch at COP31.

insights.claim: The letter ties energy transition to energy security and AI, arguing low-carbon energy cuts exposure to geopolitical and fossil price shocks and should power AI and digital infrastructure growth.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Energy-security framing links clean power to AI-power demand.
insights.locator: Low-carbon energy is becoming a strategic economic advantage
